messages:
Marta Li: Heads up — after the continuous-batcher heuristic roll (canary->prod) around 1993456780 we started seeing p95 spikes on small request workloads. Noticing throughput drop on a subset of pods. Debugging — any quick eyes?
Samir Patel: saw similar on internal smoke tests. p50 ok, p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 up to ~1.2s. Throughput down ~18% for short sequences (<=64 tokens).
Kevin Nguyen: did a quick flame/alloc profile on an affected pod — kernel selection flipped from `fast-fp16-kernel` to a `generic-int8-fallback` for many 1-4 item microbatches. Batch formation is creating a lot of tiny batches with padded seqlen => kernel mismatch. Stack snippet: ```kernel_select() -> score_kernels_for(shape) -> fallback_to_generic()```
Marta Li: Also seeing KV cache miss rate increase. Prefix cache hit rate dropped ~27% and cache management CPU spiked. Hypothesis: batching window delay causes more unique prefixes in-flight which evict entries faster, thrashing the KV.
Samir Patel: repro steps that reliably show it: run loadgen with mix: 70% short (<=64), 30% long (>=512). With new heuristic we end up with many tiny batches. Old heuristic grouped short requests more often. Queue policy seems to bias toward not delaying long requests which starves shorts.
E2 Deploy Bot: Deploy 2026-03-10T12:34:56Z rolled config: `continuous-batcher.window_ms=8 -> 12`, `token_budget_target=0.65 -> 0.55`.
Aisha Romero: quick mitigation idea: revert continuous-batcher.window_ms to 8 and raise `token_budget_target` a bit (to 0.7) to encourage larger batches. If we revert canary it should restore earlier kernel choices.
Kevin Nguyen: small patch idea for kernel selector: add a guard that prefers the fast kernel when `batch_shape.total_tokens <= 128` and `batch_size <= 8` even if quantization score slightly favors generic. Pseudocode: `if (total_tokens<=128 && batch_size<=8 && est_fast < 1.25*est_generic) pick_fast();` Microbench shows fast kernel still wins in most of these shapes.
Samir Patel: also recommend tuning queue policy: detect "short_seq" at admission and prioritize when queue length > threshold OR if add_time > X ms. That avoids starving shorts when mixed workload present.
Marta Li: Action items: 1) Aisha to revert prod canary now. 2) Kevin to land kernel-selection-guard on a 5% A/B. 3) Add KV cache hit rate to batcher dashboards + alert if hit rate drops >10%. 4) If rollback required, run postmortem. Dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/batching?exp=1993 (internal).
Aisha Romero: reverting canary flag now -> :spinner: ... Done. Rolling back to `continuous-batcher.window_ms=8` and `token_budget_target=0.65` on canary group. Monitoring metrics.
E2 Deploy Bot: Rollback completed at 1993456795 on group `canary-2`.
Samir Patel: after rollback p95 on canary pods back down to ~150ms, throughput +12%. KV cache hit returned to prior levels in the next minute. Will run longer soak and report.
Kevin Nguyen: I'll open the PR for kernel-selection-guard: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4042 — includes microbench and perf numbers: fast kernel latency 20-40% better for shapes <=128 tokens and small batch sizes.
Marta Li: thanks team. Keep this thread updated with soak numbers / any other anomalies. If other pods still show regression tag me and we can escalate.
